content:
Arthritis and frailty can shrink your world. Social prescribing aims to widen it again, at a pace that works for you.

This guide explains what social prescribing is and how to use it. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What social prescribing is

A link worker spends time with you to understand what matters to you, then helps you connect with local groups, activities and services. It works alongside medical care, not instead of it.

What it might link you to

  • Gentle exercise or walking groups.
  • Lunch clubs and social groups.
  • Benefits or money advice.
  • Volunteering or hobbies.
  • Community transport.

How to ask

Ask your GP practice whether they have a social prescribing link worker. Names and arrangements vary across England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

Making it work with arthritis and frailty

  • Mention pain, stiffness and tiredness so suggestions fit.
  • Ask about access, seating and toilets.
  • Ask about transport.
  • Start with one small thing.

Libraries as a place to go

  • Local libraries can be a warm, free and accessible place to get out and meet people.
  • Many run reading groups, coffee mornings, digital help sessions and talks.
  • Some offer home delivery of books.
  • Check accessibility, seating and toilets before your first visit.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Do I need to be referred?

Usually you ask your GP practice; some areas accept self-referral.

Is it only for loneliness?

No. It can help with many non-medical needs.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS England: Social prescribing
  • Age UK: Understanding frailty
